content.text: Abnorm opening in atrial septum b/n Rt & Lt atrium
•high-pressure oxygenated LA → low-pressure deoxygenated RA - MC → RA hypertrophy & RV dilate
•trivial & sm often close spont in infancy w ⍉sequelae - mod/lrg → Sxtomatic over time
•most sm & aSx - found via murmur on routine exam or incidental echo
(CVA from venous clots) or dysrhythmias later in life
•long-standing Lt → Rt shunt → pulm HTN (pulm arteriopathy - ⍉PS) → Eisenmenger syndrome
-USU grade 1-2 - ↑flow across PV ← RV vol overload from Lt → Rt shunt
-often ⍉loud enough to hear - ← ↑flow across PV · ⍉flow thru defect
wide fixed split S2 ⍉vary w respirations
•Crochetage sign (notching of peak of R wave in inferior leads)
•norm in uncomp sm shunt · mod/lrg → prolonged QRS + rSr' or rsR' in V1
•Percut transcatheter device closure - preferred for persistent defects w indications (Rt ♡ enlrg · pulm overcirculation)
•IE prophylaxis only w.in 6mo of repair w prosthetic material/device or residual defect @ or adjacent to prosthetic
•competitive sports 3-6mo after closure if norm pulm pressure & ventricular funct · ⍉dysrhythmias
Persistent communication b/n descending thoracic aorta & main pulm a. after birth
•USU closes w.in 48h of birth in term infants
•fetal ductus shunts blood away from pulm circ - patent >3d of life = PDA (pathologic)
•home birth ⍉RF - but premature home births may miss antenatal steroids (aid ductus closure)
•genetic syndromes: cri-du-chat · DiGeorge · Cantú · CHARGE · Noonan · Char syndrome (AD - PDA in many family members)
continued prostaglandin E2 (COX-2 mediated) prod & ↓arterial O2 content ↑patency
•after birth PVR ↓ → Lt → Rt shunt & ↑pulm blood flow
: aSx - cont flow murmur (grade 1) w norm S1/S2 - pulses norm or mildly accentuated
: exercise intol · grade 2-4 cont murmur · wide PP · displaced LV apex
: HF Sx - FTT · poor feeding · resp distress · easy fatigability · tachypnea · tachy · sweating · bounding pulses
pulm HTN & cyanotic Hdz occurring when L→R shunt switches & becomes R→L shunt (cyanotic)
-also Lt infraclavicular area - radiates to back
•resp distress · abd distention · prominent LV impulse
•progression: murmur may disappear & P2 ↑ → Rt → Lt shunt → cyanosis
•parasternal & suprasternal views - ductus connecting pulm a. & descending aorta - Doppler color flow: retrograde jet in pulm a.
: norm or cardiomegaly · ↑B/L pulm vasc markings (↑shunt vascularity - mod-lrg PDA)

: many close spont - monitor for ↑♡ workload & pulm vasc chgs → closure
•closure choice: size · age · PDA morphology · shunt & Sx
•furosemide: term infants w lrg PDA & Sxtomatic Lt → Rt shunt → HF
•Surg ligation - if medical mgnt fails esp <6kg - safe but invasive · scar · expensive
Congenital narrowing of aortic lumen @ dist or descending aorta
(80%) · MV defects · patent ductus arteriosus · Turner syndrome
•narrowing of aorta MC @ insertion of ductus arteriosus dist to origin of Lt subclavian a. → HTN in arteries prox to lesion (ex, primary arteries supplying UE) w relative ↓BP in LE
•over time, body compensates by developing collaterals around coarctation (ex, IC arteries)
: narrowing occurs dist to ductus arteriosum
: narrowing occurs prox to ductus arteriosum
May range from aSx to HF or shock after birth w closure of patent ductus arteriosus
•many aSx - often found later in childhood or adulthood
•critical CoA: presents <2wks when PDA closes - poor feeding · ⍉femoral pulses
•hallmark: ↓ or ⍉femoral pulses - UE/LE discrepancy may ⍉manifest until ductus closes
•brachial-femoral pulse delay - LE pulses diminished in severe dz
Systol murmur radiating to back · scapula or chest
•systol murmur @ Lt axilla & back - best posteriorly b/n scapulae on Lt - may extend beyond S2 or become cont
•SEM w apical ejection click if assoc BAV (systol click in most)
ddx pulsus paradoxus: ♡ tamponade · less commonly COPD · hypovolemic shock - marked ↓arterial pressure
ddx water hammer pulse: chronic AR - abrupt rapid upstroke then rapid collapse
ddx aortic dissection · supravalvular AS: also ↓BP in LE vs UE
•color-flow Doppler: visualizes defect & degree of obstruct - definitive in most
•3 sign: rounded S. aortic bulb · tight indent @ coarctation · pre- & poststenotic dilate
•⍉A. rib notching - IC a. run in grooves only along P. ribs
ddx Kerley B-lines: thin periph lines perpendicular to pleura - thickened interlobular septae - pulm edema
•neonates w severe CoA: RVH - older children: norm or LVH
•♡ cath & angio if transcatheter intervention planned
- balloon angioplasty w or w.o stent placement
- palliative: balloon angioplasty if poor LV fx
- older children: transcatheter stent for recurr CoA
- repair if: systemic HTN ← CoA · systol gradient >20mmHg UE vs LE · sig collaterals on imaging · HF - otherwise follow clin
- maintains patent ductus arteriosus - ↓sxs & improves LE blood flow
- severe w HF: PG infusion to reopen ductus + inotropes (dopamine · milrinone)
- repair after 5y → ↑systemic HTN & myocard dysfun - exercise stress test b4 athletics
